answer.headline: Monthly long-haul passenger share and passenger departures at ANC, {F63.period}

claims.text: Over {F63.period}, ANC long-haul share ({F1.definition}) is {F1} in {F1.label} and {F31} in {F31.label}. The OLS slope is {F63} ({F63.class}). The latest-month year-over-year change ({F64.definition}) is {F64} ({F64.class}).

Over the same window, passenger departures ({F32.definition}) are {F32} in {F32.label} and {F62} in {F62.label}. The OLS slope is {F65} ({F65.class}). The latest-month year-over-year change ({F66.definition}) is {F66} ({F66.class}).

Both series repeat a summer-high, winter-low shape, so the slope is not seasonally adjusted. Long-haul share is lowest in February in each year shown ({F2}, {F14}, {F26}) and highest in August in 2024 ({F8}) and 2025 ({F20}). The window has no August 2026; within 2026 the high is {F30.label} at {F30}. Passenger departures peak in July in each year ({F38}, {F50}, {F62}). The low departure month is {F43.label} in 2024 ({F43}), {F45.label} in 2025 ({F45}), and {F57.label} in the 2026 months on file ({F57}).

Same-month passenger departures in 2025 are below 2024 in every month except November ({F54} versus {F42}). From February through July 2026, same-month departures are above 2025 ({F57} versus {F45}, {F58} versus {F46}, {F59} versus {F47}, {F60} versus {F48}, {F61} versus {F49}, {F62} versus {F50}). January 2026 is {F56} against January 2025 at {F44}. The positive full-window slope {F65} mixes a softer 2025 with a stronger stretch of 2026. The latest-month change {F66} is a same-month comparison, not a full-year result.

Same-month long-haul share in 2025 is below 2024 in January and February ({F13} versus {F1}, {F14} versus {F2}) and above 2024 from March through December. In 2026 it is above 2025 from January through May and below 2025 in June and July ({F30} versus {F18}, {F31} versus {F19}), matching the direction of {F64}. The change from {F1} to {F31} compares January with July and is not a same-season trend.

assumptions: Anchorage (ANC) is bound to Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport. Merrill Field (MRI) and the Anchorage CBSA group are not included.
The phrase long-haul seat share is answered with catalog metric long_haul_share under {F1.definition}. That is a share of passengers, not a share of seats.
Passenger departures means the catalog metric departures: {F32.definition}.
The available T-100 window is the catalog coverage span {F63.period}, passed explicitly as the analysis window.
limitations: A seat-weighted long-haul share is not a catalog metric. Weights on long_haul_share are passengers, departures, or freight. Seat share as a share of seats cannot be established here.
Passenger departures are not enplaned passengers, and they exclude cargo-only departures.
International seat share is a different metric and is not this series.
The linear slope includes seasonality and is descriptive. It is not a seasonally adjusted trend and not a forecast.
The T-100 window in this catalog ends with {F62.label}. Later months are out of coverage.
Only this passenger definition of long-haul is reported. Another distance threshold, or a freight or all-traffic scope, would be a different series.
Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured.
This is a description of activity, not a screening rank and not a valuation.
